title: Hunting basics
description: Field safety, planning, and food handling.

cards.title: Plan a legal, safe hunt
cards.summary: Before going out, check the current local season, license, area rules, weather, and your return plan. Rules change by species and place.
steps: Check the current regulations with the relevant wildlife agency when a connection is available.
Confirm permission for the land or area and carry required documents.
Tell someone your route and return time; bring navigation and weather gear.
Know the species and your safe shooting area before taking any shot.
cards.source: U.S. Forest Service firearm safety guidance

cards.title: Four firearm safety checks
cards.summary: Treat every firearm as loaded; control the muzzle; keep a finger off the trigger until ready; and know the target and what is beyond it.
steps: Handle every firearm as though loaded.
Keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, never at a person.
Keep your finger outside the trigger guard until ready to shoot.
Identify the target and what lies beyond it; if unsure, do not shoot.
cards.source: U.S. Forest Service firearm safety guidance

cards.title: Cook wild game safely
cards.summary: Use a food thermometer. FoodSafety.gov lists rabbit and venison at 160°F (71°C); local wildlife agencies may add disease-specific handling advice.
steps: Keep raw meat separate from ready-to-eat food.
Chill or preserve meat promptly after field handling.
Cook rabbit and venison to 160°F (71°C) using a thermometer.
Check current wildlife-health advice for the species and area.
